stories.title: ATP Rankings Shake-Up — Shelton No. 4, Djokovic Exits Top 10
stories.angle: The 2026 US Open reshuffled the ATP rankings: Ben Shelton reaches a career-high No. 4 (up 5 from No. 9), Frances Tiafoe returns to the top 10 at No. 8, Alexander Zverev climbs to No. 2 (9,690 pts, 1,810 behind Sinner), and Novak Djokovic drops from No. 5 to No. 12 — out of the top 10 for the first time since 2018.

stories.title: Zverev's Historical Legacy — Second German US Open Champion After Becker 1989
stories.angle: Zverev becomes just the second German man to win the US Open (after Boris Becker in 1989), and the fourth player in the Open Era to win his first two Grand Slam titles in the same calendar year. Post-match: "We went 30 years without winning a Grand Slam, and now we won two in three months."

stories.title: The Big Three Era Is Over — No Federer, Nadal or Djokovic in Top 10 for First Time Since 2002
stories.angle: Novak Djokovic's first-round US Open loss to Mariano Navone sent him from No. 5 to No. 12. For the first time since October 2002, none of Federer, Nadal or Djokovic occupy a top-10 spot. Federer retired in 2022, Nadal in 2024. The Big Three era has officially ended.

stories.title: Shelton's ATP Finals Push — No. 4 Puts Turin in Sight
stories.angle: Ben Shelton's career-high No. 4 ranking virtually locks in a spot at the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin (November). No American man has qualified since John Isner in 2018. The Asian swing is his next opportunity to build on a historic US Open run.
